findings.question: Q1
findings.finding: The FY26 guide (Jul 8: $1.46-1.52, +7.0-7.5%) still assumes 30% China / 20% rest-of-world tariffs although USTR proposed 10-12.5% on Jun 3 and imposed it from Jul 24, a cushion the CFO sized in April at ~$35m COGS / $0.07 EPS for the year; but freight (Drewry WCI $4,476/FEU, Shanghai-LA $7,352, published Sep 11), Brent ($125.44 on Oct 6 vs $76.50 on Jul 8) and EUR/USD (1.1259 on Oct 2 vs 1.1396 on Jul 8) moved against the guide since, and management calls its outlook 'prudent'; net, the new FY EPS midpoint most likely lands ~$1.525 ex-refund, 1-2c under a $1.539 consensus that has not moved in 60 days (P(midpoint >= $1.54) ~40%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance decides this name: Oct 9 2025 FY EPS raised only 2c with a soft implied Q4 -> -12.55%; Jul 8 2026 FY +4c but Q3 guide below the Street -> -2.17%; Apr 7 2026 FY raise with strong revenue -> +10.65%; Jul 10 2025 beat-and-raise -> +11.25% (sealed baseline; Q3 FY25 release).
findings.why_not_priced: FY26 consensus has sat at $1.539-1.542 for 60 days (Yahoo epsTrend) through both the Jul 24 tariff regime (worth up to ~$0.05 more in H2 by the company's own sensitivity) and the September freight/oil/EUR moves (worth roughly as much against); previews cut targets (Citi $25->22, Jefferies $27->25, Stifel $28->27) without moving EPS. If the market had netted these, estimates would have moved or a preview would quantify them; none does. My net is slightly below the stale number, and the stock's 22% drawdown shows awareness, not a number.
findings.independence: Tariff regime: Morgan Lewis 2026-07-27 (https://www.morganlewis.com/pubs/2026/07/us-administration-rebuilds-global-tariff-program-under-section-301) and the Jun 3 proposal (https://textalks.com/us-proposes-10-12-5-tariffs-over-forced-labour-import-rules-putting-textile-sourcing-on-alert/); company sensitivity: Q1 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/04/08/levi-strauss-levi-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/); costs: Drewry WCI via https://www.shipuniverse.com/?p=18311, FRED Brent and EUR/USD; Jefferies/Stifel preview (https://parameter.io/levi-strauss-levi-stock-wall-street-lowers-expectations-before-quarterly-report/). findings.finding: Q3 revenue most likely ~$1.63bn (+5.5-6%), ~1% above the $1.617bn consensus: management told the July call the 4-5% guide carried 'a couple of points' of DTC prudence and was 'more conservative on wholesale' with H2 wholesale pre-books up high single digits, it beat its Q2 guide by ~3 points, and channel data through August held (BofA card spend +4.5% YoY in Aug; US clothing stores +4.1% YoY Jun-Aug; Nike North America wholesale +9% Jun-Aug; Google 'Levis' searches +17% YoY over the quarter); Europe is the soft spot (H&M Western Europe down in Jun-Aug, PVH EMEA -6%) on an easy +3% organic compare; FX ~neutral (EUR -1.0% YoY on Q3 averages).

findings.why_not_priced: Consensus $1.6167bn (+4.75%, n=14) sits inside a range the company itself called prudent and has not been revised since July; the same habit produced a ~3-point beat in Q2. A priced beat would put consensus above the 5% top ($1.621bn); the high estimate is $1.638bn.

findings.finding: Q3 adjusted EPS excluding any refund most likely $0.37-0.39 against a $0.358 consensus at the top of the $0.34-0.36 guide: LEVI beat consensus in each of the last four quarters ($0.34 vs $0.306, $0.41 vs $0.392, $0.42 vs $0.370, $0.28 vs $0.244) and beat its own Q2 guide of $0.22-0.24 by 4c, and the $200m ASR settles in Q3; Europe promotions and freight are the risks to the 61.8% gross-margin guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats of 5-15% in each of the last four quarters produced -12.55%, +0.34%, +10.65% and -2.17%: the beat itself has not decided the move.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus at the very top of the guide shows the beat habit is partly priced; the unpriced residual is 1-3c. Fully priced, consensus would sit above $0.36.

findings.question: Q4
findings.finding: Levi paid ~$80m of IEEPA duties and at May 31 had recognised only Phase-1 refunds (the 10-Q names only Beyond Yoga as benefiting), its main entries appear reconciliation-flagged (CFO in July: the reconciliation process was 'defined... a week or so ago' and not in internal results), and CBP deployed Phase 2 for reconciliation-flagged entries on Jun 29, inside Levi's Q3 (Jun 1-Aug 30); on entry-date arithmetic ~$55-70m (~$0.11-0.14 a share after tax, ~0.8% of market cap) is likely recognised in Q3, outside guidance, and Q2's Phase-1 refund was left inside adjusted EBIT.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No LEVI precedent at this size. Peers booked refunds in overlapping quarters and their reactions split on guidance: Gap ($417m, excluded from adjusted outlook) +12.9% on 2026-08-28, AEO ($179m) -14.0% on 2026-09-10 (Yahoo daily bars).
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 EPS estimates span $0.35-0.37 (n=15), so none carries a $0.11-0.14 refund; the FY high of $1.59 may carry part. Priced, the high Q3 estimate would sit near $0.48. Phase 2 opened nine days before the July guide and after the company's internal forecast.
findings.independence: CBP Phase 2 scope and date: Thompson Hine 2026-07-29 (https://www.thompsonhine.com/insights/cbp-launches-phase-2-of-the-ieepa-tariff-refund-process-and-confirms-development-of-phase-3/); CFO remark: Q2 call (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/LEVI/Q22026); peer recognition: Gap (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000039911/000162828026059262/q22026eprexhibit991.htm) and AEO (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000919012/000119312526386510/aeo-ex99_1.htm) releases. key_questions.answer: Probably yes on recognition, uncertain on treatment. Levi paid ~$80m of IEEPA duties; at May 31 it had recognised only Phase-1 refunds and the 10-Q names only Beyond Yoga as benefiting, which fits its main entries being reconciliation-flagged; the CFO said in July the reconciliation process had been 'defined... a week or so ago' and was not in internal results; CBP deployed Phase 2 for reconciliation-flagged entries on Jun 29, inside Levi's Q3. On entry dates (Phase 2 covers unliquidated entries and those within 80 days of liquidation, roughly June 2025-February 2026 imports, when most of the duty was paid) ~$55-70m is eligible, ~$0.11-0.14 a share after tax and ~0.8% of market cap. Peers with overlapping quarters booked theirs (Gap $417m, AEO $179m, PVH $107m, Columbia ~$78m). Q2's Phase-1 refund stayed inside adjusted EBIT (no exclusion line), so inclusion in adjusted EPS is a live ~50% call; either way the market will strip it, as it did for peers whose reactions split on guidance. Priced answer: no estimate carries it.

premortem.other_way_reason: The stock falls 8-12% because the FY guide comes in at or below a pass-through (midpoint <= $1.51 ex-refund) and the implied Q4 is trimmed for freight, oil-driven consumer caution, EUR and Europe: the October 2025 pattern, when a 2c FY raise with a soft implied Q4 cost 12.55%, with the refund read as low quality and a ~1% revenue beat too small to matter.
premortem.question: Q1
premortem.evidence_already_had: Previews expecting only a slight EPS raise and a flat revenue guide (Jefferies 2026-10-01); elevated freight (Drewry WCI $4,476/FEU, Shanghai-LA $7,352, published 2026-09-11); Brent $125; EUR 1.126; H&M and PVH Europe weakness; management's own 'prudence' and its July decision to keep a 20% tariff assumption it knew was high; this name's sale of two of its last three beat-and-raise prints.

investment_decision.reason: Three of the four frozen questions come back modestly above their priced answers: Q3 revenue (~$1.63bn vs $1.617bn) and EPS (~$0.38 vs $0.358) above a guide management itself called prudent (Q2, Q3), and a ~$55-70m refund no estimate carries (Q4), on a name 22% off its high with calls bid and a rising but uncrowded short. The line it trades on (Q1, the FY guide) is a coin flip around a $1.539 consensus that already sits above the guide top, with the tariff cushion roughly cancelled by freight, oil and EUR, so the lean is small and agrees with the positive impact_sum.
investment_decision.what_would_change_it: A new FY26 adjusted EPS midpoint, ex-refund, at or below ~$1.51: the Q3 beat not passed through, or the implied Q4 cut for freight, consumer or Europe.
